data.jobspec:
#!/bin/ksh
#flux: --job-name=jaqm_fcst_v531_cs
#flux: --output=jaqm_fcst_cs.out
#flux: --error=jaqm_fcst_cs.err
#flux: --mem-per-node=3G
#flux: --time=02:30
#flux: --account=CMAQ-T2O
#flux: --nodes=24
# The LSF queue directive '-q dev' does not have a direct equivalent in Flux.
# This is typically handled by resource constraints or queue policies on the target system.
# The LSF memory request '-M 3000' (3GB) was translated to '--mem-per-node=3G'.
# The LSF directive '-cwd .' is the default behavior in Flux, so no directive is needed.
# The LSF extended scheduling directive '-extsched 'CRAYLINUX[]'' is a site-specific
# hardware request and does not have a direct Flux equivalent. It has been omitted.

source /opt/modules/default/init/ksh 
module unload PrgEnv-cray
module load PrgEnv-intel
module load iobuf
module load prod_util
module load prod_envir

export NODES=24
export IOBUF_PARAMS="12M:verbose"

set -ax

ulimit -s unlimited

export RUN_ENVIR=notnco
export COMROOT=/gpfs/hps3/ptmp/${USER}/com
export NWROOT=/u/${USER}/noscrub/nwdev
export NWROOTp1=/nwprod
export cmaq_ver=v5.3.1
export envir=para
export job=aqm_cmaq_cs
#
export PARAFLAG=YES

export SENDCOM=YES
export SENDDBN=NO
export SENDECF=NO

export FCST=YES
 
# It is assumed that the JAQM_FORECAST_CS job script will use a job launcher
# like 'flux run' internally to start processes on the allocated 24 nodes.
# If it is a serial script, this will result in 23 idle nodes.
${HOMEaqm}/jobs/JAQM_FORECAST_CS

err=$?
if [ "${PARAFLAG}" = "YES" ]
then
  if [ ${err} -ne 0 ]
  then
    exit 249
  fi
fi

reasons: The directive '--mem-per-node=3G' is not a valid Flux option.
The directive '--account=CMAQ-T2O' is not a valid Flux option.
issues: Significant Resource Waste: The job requests 24 nodes but does not specify how many tasks to run per node. It then executes a single serial script (`${HOMEaqm}/jobs/JAQM_FORECAST_CS`). This command will run on only one core of one of the allocated nodes. Unless that script contains its own MPI launcher (e.g., `flux run`), the other 23 nodes and all other cores on the first node will remain completely idle for the entire duration of the job, resulting in an extreme waste of allocated resources.

The script relies on an environment variable `$HOMEaqm` which is not defined within the script itself. The job will fail if this variable is not set in the environment from which the job is submitted.

# - Account ('-P CMAQ-T2O')
# - Memory ('-M 3000')
# --
# CRITICAL PERFORMANCE IMPLICATION:
# The original job requested 3GB of memory per node. This version will run with the system's default memory,
# which may be smaller, creating a risk the job will be terminated by the Out-Of-Memory (OOM) killer.
# --
# The LSF queue and extended scheduling directives were also omitted as they are site-specific.

source /opt/modules/default/init/ksh 
module unload PrgEnv-cray
module load PrgEnv-intel
module load iobuf
module load prod_util
module load prod_envir

export IOBUF_PARAMS="12M:verbose"

export COMROOT=/gpfs/hps3/ptmp/${USER}/com
export NWROOT=/u/${USER}/noscrub/nwdev
export NWROOTp1=/nwprod
export cmaq_ver=v5.3.1
export envir=para
export job=aqm_cmaq_cs
export PARAFLAG=YES

export SENDCOM=YES
export SENDDBN=NO
export SENDECF=NO

export FCST=YES

# WARNING: This job requests 24 nodes but launches a single serial command.
# If the 'JAQM_FORECAST_CS' script does not contain its own MPI launcher (e.g., 'flux run'),
# 23 nodes will remain idle, wasting significant resources.
${HOMEaqm}/jobs/JAQM_FORECAST_CS

err=$?
if [ "${PARAFLAG}" = "YES" ]

  if [ ${err} -ne 0 ]
  then
    exit 249
  fi

issues: Significant Resource Waste: The job requests 24 nodes but does not specify how many tasks to run per node. It then executes a single serial script (`${HOMEaqm}/jobs/JAQM_FORECAST_CS`). This command will run on only one core of one of the allocated nodes. Unless that script contains its own MPI launcher (e.g., `flux run`), the other 23 nodes and all other cores on the first node will remain completely idle for the entire duration of the job, resulting in an extreme waste of allocated resources.

Critical Performance Risk: The original job requested 3GB of memory per node, but this version omits any memory request. The job will run with the system's default memory allocation. There is a high probability that the application will exceed this limit and be terminated by the system's Out-Of-Memory (OOM) killer, causing the job to fail.

Potential for Rejection: The original job specified an account (`-P CMAQ-T2O`), which was omitted. On many HPC systems, an account is a mandatory field for job submission for accounting and fair-share purposes. Submitting this job without an account may lead to immediate rejection by the scheduler.

The script relies on an environment variable `$HOMEaqm` which is not defined within the script itself. The job will fail with a 'command not found' error if this variable is not set in the environment from which the job is submitted.
